about: A Zork II style underground empire: a barrow, a cavern, a carousel room, the Wizard's illusions, a riddle door, a dragon, and the Bank of Zork. Several routes end at soft walls that say the rest will have to wait.

done.why: The dragon would not be hurt by my sword. The ice, the lava tube, the rockfall and the crack were all blocked. I could not find a way forward, so I stopped.

moments.note: The Wizard's illusion made a gold ingot that could not be taken. The room explained the trick itself.
The Carousel Room scrambles directions. I could not tell whether I was making progress or just getting random exits.
Saying 'well' to the riddle opened the stone door.
The bank vault area: an alarm blocked me when I carried the portrait, and the viewing room gave me nothing to do.
Several paths ended with 'will have to wait': the lava tube, the rockfall and the ice. The world has visible edges.
Attacking the dragon only got 'surprised and interested', with no sign of how to beat it.

wished: A hint about what the viewing room or the vault wants from me.
A way to get past the dragon.
A clearer way to navigate the Carousel Room.

lines.line: The room, having no say in the matter, let it, and has the grace to look embarrassed about it now.
lines.why: Funny and well written. It dissolves the illusion and keeps the tone.

lines.line: There is a curtain of light there. It is not the kind of thing one goes north through; it is the kind of thing one goes through.
lines.why: A gentle nudge that points at the right verb.

fun.why: Familiar Zork II puzzles with some fresh touches, but I hit several dead ends.

engagement.why: I had an early goal, but the way forward got unclear.

difficulty.why: The Carousel Room and the dragon had me stuck. The riddle was easy.

interestingness.why: The Wizard's illusions are a fresh layer on a classic map.

prose.why: Strong custom lines mixed with classic descriptions.
